problem:
From **left to right**, the ellipse $25{x}^{2}+14{y}^{2}-50x-11y=29$ intercepts the $x$-axis at the points $A$ and $B.$ Find the coordinates of these points.

$A($
{{field-1}}
$,$
{{field-2}}$)\,$

and 

$\,B($
{{field-3}}$,$
{{field-4}}
$)$
worked_solution:
To calculate the $x$-intercepts, we need to substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the ellipse and solve the resulting equation for $x.$ We do this and solve the resulting equation by completing the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}25{x}^{2}+14{y}^{2}-50x-11y & =29 \\ 25{x}^{2}+14(0)^{2}-50x-11(0) & =29 \\ 25{x}^{2}-50x & =29 \\ {x}^{2}-2x & =\frac{29}{25} \\ (x-1)^{2}-{1}^{2} & =\frac{29}{25} \\ (x-1)^{2} & =\frac{29}{25}+1 \\ (x-1)^{2} & =\frac{29}{25}+\frac{25}{25} \\ (x-1)^{2} & =\frac{54}{25} \\ x-1 & =\pm \frac{3\sqrt{6}}{5} \\ x & =1\pm \frac{3\sqrt{6}}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, from left to right, the $x$-intercepts are

$$
A(1-\frac{3\sqrt{6}}{5},0)\,\text{and}\,B(1+\frac{3\sqrt{6}}{5},0).
$$
